messages.subject: Dimethyl Labeled Sample Design
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats,

We have a dataset that, for historical reasons in our lab, was collected with DDA and dimethyl labeling. For those who don't know, dimethyl labeling is a stable isotopic labeling strategy used for MS1 quantification in a similar manner to SILAC.  See here <http://www.nature.com/nprot/journal/v4/n4/full/nprot.2009.21.html> for more details.

Our experiment consists of mouse tissue from wildtype (WT) and knockout (KO) animals at 3 separate timepoints (T1, T2 and T3) each with multiple biological replicates. However, each run consists of one WT and one KO mouse sample that were dimethyl labeled and combined. We've used MaxQuant to analyze these runs, resulting intensities for the heavy and light channels per protein per run. I've tried to illustrate our experimental design in the table below:

Run | Condition (Heavy) | Condition (Light) | Age | BioReplicate
-----------------------------------------------------------------
1   | KO                | WT                | T1  | 1
2   | KO                | WT                | T1  | 2
3   | KO                | WT                | T1  | 3
4   | KO                | WT                | T2  | 1
5   | KO                | WT                | T2  | 2
6   | KO                | WT                | T2  | 3
7   | KO                | WT                | T3  | 1
8   | KO                | WT                | T3  | 2
9   | KO                | WT                | T3  | 3

Can we use MSstats to make inferences about WT vs KO  at each age as well as compare WT between ages separately from KO between ages?  If this is possible, how should I format my annotation file for MaxQtoMSstatsFormat()? My thought for how to set-up the annotation file is below.

Raw.file | Condition | BioReplicate | Experiment | IsotopLabelType
------------------------------------------------------------------
file1    | WT        | 1            | T1         | L
file2    | WT        | 2            | T1         | L
file3    | WT        | 3            | T1         | L
file4    | WT        | 1            | T2         | L
...
file1    | KO        | 1            | T1         | H
file2    | KO        | 2            | T1         | H
...

Thank you for your help.

Best,
Will

messages.subject: Re: Dimethyl Labeled Sample Design
messages.body_plain:
Update:

With some exploring I found that there is an unimplemented option in MaxQtoMSstatsFormat() called "experiment" (possibly due to known issues?). I decided to enable the option in my own copy of the function with the value "SILAC" and the format conversion seemed to work, though I haven't verified thoroughly. I also used a slightly different annotation file after further consulting the documentation. This version looks like, where experiment matches the experiment name in MaxQuant:

Raw.file | Condition | BioReplicate | Experiment | IsotopLabelType
------------------------------------------------------------------

file1    | WT_T1     | 1            | WT_T1_1    | L
file2    | WT_T1     | 2            | WT_T1_2    | L
file3    | WT_T1     | 3            | WT_T1_3    | L
file4    | WT_T2     | 1            | WT_T2_1    | L
...
file1    | KO_T1     | 1            | KO_T1_1    | H
file2    | KO_T1     | 2            | KO_T1_2    | H
...

I'm currently attempting to process in MSstats this. As long as I set up contrasts correctly, will this yield statistically valid results?

Best,
Will

messages.subject: Error when processing data
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats team:

I am trying to using MSstats for some DIA data with PTMs. I got the reports from Spectronaut and transfer to MSstats input. What I am focusing is peptide level quantification, so I rename the same protein with different PTMs. However, when I am processing the data, it keeps on complaining about  missing intensities.

Here is the error message:

"CAUTION : some REFERENCE features have missing intensities in all the runs. The completely missing REFERENCE features are _NA_NA_NA, AAAAAAAAAAGAAGGRGS[+80]GPGR_2_NA_0, AAAAAAAGAAGSAAPAAAAGAPGS[+80]GGAPSGSQGVLIGDR_2_NA_0, AAAAAAAGAAGSAAPAAAAGAPGSGGAPS[+80]GSQGVLIGDR_2_NA_0, AAAAAAAGAAGSAAPAAAAGAPGSGGAPSGS[+80]QGVLIGDR_2_NA_0, AAAAAAAGDS[+80]DS[+80]WDADAFSVEDPVRK_2_NA_0, AAAAAAAGDS[+80]DSWDADAFSVEDPVR_2_NA_0, AAAAAAAGDSDS[+80]WDADAFSVEDPVRK_2_NA_0, Grand Total_NA_NA_NA. Please check whether features in the list are correctly generated from spectral processing tool.

CAUTION : some ENDOGENOUS features have missing intensities in all the runs. The completely missing ENDOGENOUS features are _NA_NA_NA, Grand Total_NA_NA_NA. Please check whether features in the list are correctly generated from spectral processing tool.

 DONE : Incomplete rows for missing peaks are added with intensity values=NA.

Error in factor(work$RUN, levels = unique(work$RUN), labels = seq(1, length(unique(work$RUN)))) :
  invalid 'labels'; length 10 should be 1 or 9"

Attached the Test file.

Can you please help me have a look what's wrong with the input file?

Thanks a lot for your help. Appreciate it.

Cheers
Cheng

Hi Adrien,

When you run each of the MSstats in Skyline, a corresponding output file containing the values for visualization will be generated under the same folder:

MSstats QC - dataProcessedData.csv

MSstats Group Comparison - TestingResult.csv

MSstats Design Sample Size - SampleSizeCalculation.csv

Best,
Tsung-Heng

Unfortunately, MSstats does not support for experiments in which each run has more than two samples from different conditions with different labeling, such as SILAC, iTRAQ, TMT.

- Meena

messages.body_plain:
Hi Cheng,

There's something wrong in your input data. There are 110091 rows but only the first 63 rows have valid entries. Check for example the following
raw <- read.csv("test.csv")
dim(raw)
raw[61:70, ]
tail(raw)

You can also open the CSV file with EXCEL and check the 110091st row. It may be helpful to double check what's going on during signal processing and data conversion.

HTH
Tsung-Heng

messages.subject: Re: No imputation
messages.body_plain:
Dear Cheng,

quant$ProcessedData : reeformatted and normalized data. It does not include imputed values.
quant$RunlevelData : summarized values after imputation.

Please check the manual, (msstats.org <http://msstats.org> > workflow > user manual for MSstats) for normalization options. and other documentations are also available in msstats.org <http://msstats.org>.

Hope to help.

Sincerely,
- Meena
